heroCommands.comment: Generate speech through the local API

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Voicebox is a local-first AI voice studio. It clones voices from a few seconds of audio, generates speech in 23 languages with 8 text-to-speech engines, lets you dictate into any app, and gives AI agents a voice through MCP, all running on your own machine.
sixtySeconds.problem: Cloud voice tools send your voice data to someone else's servers and charge per use. Voicebox positions itself as a free, open-source alternative to ElevenLabs (speech output) and WisprFlow (dictation) in one app, with models and recordings staying on your machine.
whoFor: Creators making narration, podcasts or audiobooks
Developers giving agents like Claude Code a voice
Anyone wanting a local alternative to cloud voice services
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a polished desktop app that covers both voice output and voice input locally. Linux has no pre-built binaries yet.
requirements: macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) or Windows for the desktop app
Linux: build from source, or Docker
A GPU helps but CPU works

overview: Voicebox bundles eight TTS engines, including Qwen3-TTS, Chatterbox Multilingual, Chatterbox Turbo, LuxTTS, HumeAI TADA and Kokoro, switchable per generation. You can clone a voice from a reference sample or use 50+ preset voices, add effects like reverb and pitch shift, and build multi-voice conversations in a Stories timeline editor. Long texts are chunked and crossfaded automatically.

The other half is voice input: a global dictation hotkey with Whisper-based speech-to-text and optional cleanup by a bundled local LLM. On macOS the transcript pastes straight into the focused text field.

A REST API on port 17493 and a built-in MCP server let apps and agents generate speech, speak in a cloned voice and transcribe audio. It's built with Tauri (Rust) and supports Apple MLX, CUDA, ROCm, DirectML, Intel Arc and CPU.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from Voicebox's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Download the DMG
steps.body: Apple Silicon and Intel builds are on voicebox.sh and the GitHub releases page.

steps.title: Download the MSI installer
steps.body: From voicebox.sh or the GitHub releases page.

steps.title: Install prerequisites
steps.body: Bun, Rust, Python 3.12, the Tauri prerequisites and just (brew install just or cargo install just).

steps.title: Clone and set up
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/jamiepine/voicebox.git
cd voicebox
just setup

steps.title: Start the backend and desktop app

firstRun.title: List your voice profiles through the API

tutorial.title: Give Claude Code a voice
tutorial.useCase: Connect Voicebox's MCP server so your coding agent can speak to you in a voice you choose.

steps.title: Add the MCP server
steps.code:
claude mcp add voicebox \
  --transport http \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:17493/mcp \
  --header "X-Voicebox-Client-Id: claude-code"

steps.title: Pick the agent's voice
steps.body: In Voicebox, open Settings, then MCP, and bind Claude Code to a voice profile.

steps.title: Test speech from a script
steps.code:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:17493/speak \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Voicebox-Client-Id: my-script" \
  -d '{"text": "Deploy complete.", "profile": "Morgan"}'

tutorial.expected: The agent gains voicebox_speak, voicebox_transcribe, voicebox_list_captures and voicebox_list_profiles tools, and a pill shows the voice name whenever it speaks.
nextSteps: Read the full API docs at http://127.0.0.1:17493/docs
